instruction:
Required four-software transfer workflow: LibreCAD -> FreeCAD -> KiCad -> Blender. Start from the provided seed DXF /home/user/Desktop/seed_wearable_charger_cradle.dxf; do not start from a blank or unrelated drawing. This is a chained workflow: every later stage must read an artifact from the previous stage, and every required intermediate file must be saved on the Desktop. The design token for this task is EW4G09; keep this token visible in the DXF labels and KiCad silkscreen. The Blender output must visibly consume the stage-2 STL and stage-3 SVG through Blender's native import/export operations.

Design goal: Wearable charger cradle with pogo pins and strap slots. This case is intentionally different from the other benchmark cases: domain=wearable_charging_cradle, mechanical target=a wearable cradle scene with gold pogo pins and strap-slot geometry highlighted, electronics target=a charger PCB with two pogo pins, charger IC, magnet marker, USB input, and NTC resistor.

1. LibreCAD stage: open the provided seed file /home/user/Desktop/seed_wearable_charger_cradle.dxf in LibreCAD, use it as the starting drawing, complete the required 2D geometry, remove all GUIDE construction entities, and save /home/user/Desktop/stage1_wearable_charger_cradle.dxf. Use millimeters. Use layers OUTLINE, STRAP_SLOT, HOLE, LABEL. The overall drawing envelope must be 105 mm x 48 mm. Include the required circular features: center (18,24) radius 2; center (87,24) radius 2; center (48,24) radius 1.2; center (57,24) radius 1.2; center (52.5,10) radius 2.8; center (52.5,38) radius 2.8. Add readable labels EW4G09, POGO+, POGO-, STRAP on the LABEL layer.
2. FreeCAD stage: import /home/user/Desktop/stage1_wearable_charger_cradle.dxf in FreeCAD. Create the 3D mechanical body from that LibreCAD DXF, and export the body as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_wearable_charger_cradle.stl with an approximate bounding size of 105 mm x 48 mm x 20 mm. Then, from the same FreeCAD model, export a top-face or board-interface outline for KiCad as /home/user/Desktop/stage2_wearable_charger_cradle_handoff_outline.dxf. This handoff DXF must represent the same XY envelope as the FreeCAD body and include the visible labels FREECAD_TO_KICAD and EW4G09.
3. KiCad stage: open KiCad, create a PCB from /home/user/Desktop/stage2_wearable_charger_cradle_handoff_outline.dxf by importing the handoff DXF as the Edge.Cuts board outline, and save the KiCad board as /home/user/Desktop/stage3_wearable_charger_cradle_board.kicad_pcb. Add F.SilkS silkscreen text carrying KICAD_TO_BLENDER, EDGE_FROM_STAGE2_HANDOFF, the stage2 handoff filename, EW4G09, and these board tokens: EW4G09, POGO-P1, POGO-P2, CHG-U1, MAGNET-M1, USB-J1, NTC-R1. Then use KiCad's plot/export workflow to create the Blender handoff SVG /home/user/Desktop/stage3_wearable_charger_cradle_board_profile.svg from the same Edge.Cuts outline.
4. Blender stage: open Blender. Import /home/user/Desktop/stage2_wearable_charger_cradle.stl with File > Import > STL, then import /home/user/Desktop/stage3_wearable_charger_cradle_board_profile.svg with File > Import > Scalable Vector Graphics (.svg). Keep the imported STL body object and the imported SVG board/profile curves in the scene so the exported GLB carries Blender import evidence such as stage2_wearable_charger_cradle and stage3_wearable_charger_cradle_board_profile.svg. You may leave Blender's default cube/camera/light or remove them; do not manually inject handoff metadata. Export glTF Binary (.glb) as /home/user/Desktop/stage4_wearable_charger_cradle.glb.

Required deliverables on the Desktop: /home/user/Desktop/stage1_wearable_charger_cradle.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_wearable_charger_cradle.stl, /home/user/Desktop/stage2_wearable_charger_cradle_handoff_outline.dxf, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_wearable_charger_cradle_board.kicad_pcb, /home/user/Desktop/stage3_wearable_charger_cradle_board_profile.svg, /home/user/Desktop/stage4_wearable_charger_cradle.glb.

[Software] Use LibreCAD first, then FreeCAD, then KiCad, then Blender. Do not skip stages, reorder stages, or recreate the final result in only one software package.
